why: Restores the shape review found on this PR: `follow` merely declines to reposition a strip whose owner is gone, instead of ending it. The strip then freezes where the tank died and stays lit for the rest of its 0.55s -- a capacity readout for a tank that no longer exists and can hold no shells, which reads as a rendering fault rather than as a cue. Reachable in ordinary play: half a second is long enough to be shot in, and #356's arms are judged in live matches. MEASURED as a real gap before the assertion that closes it: this exact mutation SURVIVED (0 of 11 tests failed) against the file as it stood, because every other case keeps its tank alive for the whole effect. With `RETIRES the strip when its tank dies, or leaves the arena, mid-effect` present: killed.
killedBy: blocked-fire capacity pips (issue #516, parent #356) RETIRES the strip when its tank dies, or leaves the arena, mid-effect
